title: API Contingency Workflow Drafts
content:
Scope and purpose:
This is a working draft of contingency procedures for common API failure modes we see in production: request timeouts, elevated 429 (rate-limit) responses, degraded streaming (intermittent chunking or stalled streams), and sudden spike in 5xx error rate. The goal is to provide an operator-friendly checklist that balances fast mitigation (keep customers online) with low-impact changes (avoid cascading failures).

When to use this doc:
- Pager triggers for API error-rate alerts (error-rate > 3% on production routes sustained for > 5m).
- Latency SLO breaches (p50/p95/p99 for text-generation routes degrade beyond configured thresholds).
- Streaming health alerts: egress stalls or client read-timeout spikes.
- Rate-limit storms indicated by sudden surge in 429s tied to one or more API keys or routes.

High-level principles (operator guidance):
1) Limit blast radius: prefer configuration-level mitigations (route throttles, model fallbacks) to infra-wide reboots.
2) Prioritize customer-facing continuity: enable graceful degradation (smaller model, reduced max_tokens) before taking routes offline.
3) Avoid broad cache/cdn purges during incidents unless they clearly correlate.
4) Communicate early and often: update incident channel with short bullets every 10–20 minutes.

Quick triage script (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm alert: open the SRE -> API Health dashboard, check the alert rule that fired and note the affected route(s), model id(s), and regions.
2) Look for correlated signals:
   - Ingress metrics: request rate, client IP concentration, auth key usage.
   - Worker metrics: queue backlog, GPU utilization, OOM/oom_killer logs.
   - Router metrics: connection churn, keepalive failures, TLS handshake errors.
   - Upstream model health: model-server latencies and error logs.
3) Determine scope: global vs region vs customer-key scoped. Add "scope=global|region|key" to the incident summary.
4) If 429s predominate: run per-key rate breakdown (see commands below).

Operator checklist (stepwise):
- COLLECTION: capture context before changing systems
  - Mark incident in incident tracker (JIRA ticket stub SRE-INC-YYYY-NNN).
  - Take screenshots of dashboards, save a short tail of relevant logs (last 1–5k lines).
  - Note exact alert thresholds and timestamps.

- MITIGATION: low-risk actions first
  1) Apply aggressive retry-window headers to clients (if client library supports), and communicate to SDK teams to temporarily reduce client concurrency.
  2) Enable per-tenant throttles for noisy keys: set a temporary per-key qps cap in the routing layer (recommended: cap to 50–75% of normal for the offending key).
  3) Turn on incremental degradation: reduce default max_tokens and temperature for non-critical endpoints to reduce compute per request.
  4) For streaming stalls: flip the stream-buffer-mode from "auto-batch" to "flush-eager" for the affected route to sacrifice some throughput for lower streaming tail latency.

- ESCALATION: when to involve other teams
  - If queue backlog persists after 5 minutes of mitigations, page serving-runtime and infra on-call.
  - If GPU OOMs or driver crashes are present, escalate to infra (release-engineering) immediately.
  - If a single customer key is causing sustained >60% of errors and they are a high-touch account, loop in account's SE and solutions-eng.

Concrete diagnostic commands (internal CLI examples):
- per-key request breakdown (last 10m): rcli metrics query --metric=requests.count --filter="route=chat*" --group-by=api_key --since=10m
- top error traces: rcli logs tail --service=router --filter="level>=error" --since=15m --limit=200
- streaming backpressure check: rcli inspect stream_pool --route=stream.chat --metrics=buffer_len,blocked_ticks
- worker queue depth: rcli metrics query --metric=worker.queue.depth --group-by=pool --since=5m
(These are example commands; adapt if the tool returns an error.)

Mitigation recipes (by failure mode):
1) Timeouts (many 504s / client read timeouts)
  - Quick fix: temporarily lower per-request max_seq_length and enforce early response heuristics (e.g., return partial responses with a warning token).
  - Medium-term: enable prefix caching for frequent prompts (routes with high cache-hit potential).
  - If caused by slow upstream model: failover to a compatible, faster model variant (model-fallback mapping can be modified in the routing policy).

2) Elevated 429s (rate limiting storms)
  - Quick fix: apply per-key emergency throttles and increase global token-bucket burst windows for SLAs while throttling best-effort keys.
  - Find source: check for sudden client-side retry loops (look for repeated identical request hashes). If present, apply stricter idempotency validation or instruct SDK teams to disable aggressive retries.
  - If 429s are due to capacity depletion: bring up burst capacity pool for Dedicated customers only after approval from infra (note cost impact).

3) Degraded streaming (chunk delays, stalls)
  - Quick fix: alter routing to route new streams to a healthy region/cluster; if not possible, enable shorter stream flush intervals.
  - Reduce batching windows for streaming workers, even if throughput drops.
  - If network between edge and worker shows packet loss, enable TCP keepalive tuning and consider moving traffic to alternate peering.

4) Elevated 5xx error rate
  - If 5xxs are concentrated in one deployment shard: remove shard from the routing pool (drain) and route traffic to adjacent capacity.
  - If 5xxs are application-level (stack traces show NPEs or decode errors), roll back the last config/feature flag that touched the route.
  - If dependent external service failing (e.g., KMS, metrics exporter): enable degraded-mode that bypasses non-critical external calls.

Communication template (post to incident channel):
- Short summary line (what, where, impact).
- Actions taken so far (bulleted).
- Next steps and owner for each.
- ETA for next update (10–20m).
Example: "[Incident] 2026-02-20 15:12 UTC - elevated 429s on /v1/chat (us-west-2). Impact: 30% of requests receiving 429. Actions: applied per-key caps to top 3 noisy keys, reduced default max_tokens to 512, engaged infra. Next update in 15m. Owner: Jordan K."

Post-incident follow-up (must do before closing):
- Expand the incident ticket with root-cause analysis, timeline, and artifacts (screenshots, logs).
- Propose at least two preventive actions (e.g., add a per-tenant early-warning alert, tune default batching policy).
- Schedule a short blameless review (30–45m) with SRE + serving-runtime + SDK owners within 7 days.

Examples / Scenario walkthroughs (quick references):
- Scenario A: sudden spike of 429s originating from a single api key due to a runaway retry loop in old SDK.
  - Detect: per-key qps spike, identical request hash pattern, user-agent old-sdk-1.2.
  - Mitigate: emergency per-key cap, contact SDK team to push patch, add alert for repeated identical hashes.

- Scenario B: progressive streaming degradation after model upgrade (p95 chunk latency rising but overall throughput steady).
  - Detect: p50 ok, p95/p99 for stream chunk time increases; workers report larger buffer_len.
  - Mitigate: rollback model to previous variant, enable flush-eager on the route, and open a rollout SR for model profiling.

Open questions / TODOs for this draft:
- Default per-key emergency caps: what should be the standard values for free-tier vs enterprise? (charge owners: product + revenue ops).
- SDK backoff guidance update: unify recommended client retry strategies across languages (owner: devexp).
- Add automated postmortem template in Confluence and link to ticket creation flow (owner: eng-sre).

Appendix: useful dashboards and alerts (links internal):
- API Health Overview: dashboards/redwood/api-health
- Streaming Latency Explorer: dashboards/redwood/streaming-latency
- Per-key Traffic Map: dashboards/redwood/per-key-qps
- Alert rules: alerts/api-error-rate, alerts/stream-stall, alerts/per-key-429-spike

Notes to self (operator shorthand):
- When in doubt, prefer model-fallback over cluster-wide restarts.
- Keep incident messages short; long form goes in ticket.
- Save any executed CLI commands in the ticket body so we can replay diagnostics later.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05: initial draft (Jordan K)
- 2025-12-10: added streaming flush guidance (Priya D)
- 2026-02-20: clarified per-key cap policy and commands (Evan M)

End of draft.
